lessons.title: It's too small!
lessons.goal_uz: Do'konda kiyim tanlaysiz, o'lcham so'raysiz va "too big / not big enough" bilan muammoni tushuntirasiz.

words.ex: Can I try on this jacket?
The fitting room is over there.

lines.en: Hello, can I help you?
lines.uz: Salom, yordam bera olamanmi?

lines.en: Yes, I'm looking for a winter jacket. Can I try on this one?
lines.uz: Ha, qishki kurtka qidiryapman. Mana shunisini kiyib ko'rsam bo'ladimi?

lines.en: Of course. What size are you?
lines.uz: Albatta. O'lchamingiz qanaqa?

lines.en: Medium, I think. Where's the fitting room?
lines.uz: Medium, menimcha. Kiyinish xonasi qayerda?

lines.en: Hmm, it's too tight. It isn't big enough. Have you got it in large?
lines.uz: Hmm, tor ekan. Yetarlicha katta emas. Large o'lchami bormi?

lines.en: Yes, here you are. And it's in the sale — only 450,000 som.
lines.uz: Ha, marhamat. Va u chegirmada — atigi 450 ming so'm.

lines.en: Perfect. It's warm enough for winter, and it isn't too expensive. I'll take it.
lines.uz: Zo'r. Qish uchun yetarlicha issiq, juda qimmat ham emas. Olaman.

steps.q: What was the problem with the first jacket?
steps.explain_uz: "it's too tight. It isn't big enough."

steps.q: Why does Madina buy the large jacket?
options: It's warm and not too expensive.

steps.body_uz:
**too + sifat** — "haddan tashqari, juda (ortiqcha)" — salbiy ma'no: It's **too** expensive. (Sotib ololmayman.)
**very** esa shunchaki "juda": It's **very** expensive, but I can buy it.
**sifat + enough** — "yetarlicha". enough sifatdan **keyin** keladi: big **enough**, warm **enough**. ("enough big" — xato!)
Inkor: It is**n't** big **enough** = It's too small.
**enough + ot** — otdan oldin: I haven't got **enough money**.

examples.en: These shoes are too small for me.
Is this coat warm enough for winter?
examples.uz: Bu palto qish uchun yetarlicha issiqmi?

examples.en: I can't buy it — I haven't got enough money.
He isn't old enough to drive.
examples.uz: U mashina haydash uchun hali yosh.

lessons.title: Have you done the dishes yet?
lessons.goal_uz: Uy ishlari haqida gapirasiz va hozirgacha qilingan ishlarni Present Perfect (just, already, yet) bilan aytasiz.

words.ex: I always do the dishes after dinner.
Mum does the laundry on Sundays.
Can you take out the rubbish?
Our guests are coming at seven.

steps.title: Guests are coming!
steps.context_uz: Kechqurun mehmonlar keladi. Ona bolalaridan ishlar qanday ketayotganini so'rayapti.

lines.en: The guests are coming at seven! Have you tidied the living room yet?
lines.uz: Mehmonlar soat yettida keladi! Mehmonxonani yig'ishtirdingizmi?

lines.en: Yes, I've already tidied it. And I've just vacuumed the carpet.
lines.uz: Ha, allaqachon yig'ishtirdim. Gilamni ham hozirgina changyutgich bilan tozaladim.

lines.en: Great! Bekzod, have you done the dishes?
lines.uz: Zo'r! Bekzod, idishlarni yuvdingmi?

lines.en: Not yet, Mum. I've just finished my homework.
lines.uz: Hali yo'q, oyi. Uy vazifamni endigina tugatdim.

lines.en: OK, do them now, please. And take out the rubbish.
lines.uz: Mayli, hozir yuvib qo'y. Axlatni ham chiqar.

lines.en: Has Dad bought the bread yet?
lines.uz: Dadam nonni oldimi?

lines.en: Yes, he's already bought it. He's just come home.
lines.uz: Ha, allaqachon oldi. Hozirgina uyga keldi.

steps.explain_uz: "I've already tidied it... I've just vacuumed".

steps.body_uz:
Tuzilma: **have / has + V3** (3-shakl): I **have** clean**ed**, she **has** do**ne**, he **has** bought.
Natija hozir muhim, vaqt aytilmaydi (yesterday, last week bilan ishlatilmaydi!).
**just** — "hozirgina": I've **just** finished. (have va V3 orasida)
**already** — "allaqachon" (kutilganidan oldin): She's **already** gone.
**yet** — "hali / ...dimi?" faqat **inkor va savolda**, gap **oxirida**: Have you eaten **yet**? I haven't finished **yet**.
Qisqa javob: Yes, I **have**. / No, I **haven't**. / Not yet.

examples.en: I've just made some tea. Do you want some?
Have you done the laundry yet?
He hasn't ironed his shirt yet.

options: I have cleaned my room yesterday.
steps.explain_uz: **yesterday** — aniq vaqt → Past Simple. Present Perfect aniq vaqt bilan ishlatilmaydi.

steps.context_uz: Shahzoda va akasi Ulug'bek samsa qilmoqchi. Avval uyda nima borligini tekshirishyapti.

lines.en: OK, the recipe says one kilo of flour. How much flour have we got?
lines.uz: Xo'sh, retseptda bir kilo un deyilgan. Bizda qancha un bor?

lines.en: Not much. Only a little — maybe 300 grams.
lines.uz: Ko'p emas. Ozgina — balki 300 gramm.

lines.en: And how many onions have we got?
lines.uz: Piyoz-chi, nechta bor?

lines.en: Only a few. Three, I think. We need a lot of onions for samsa.
lines.uz: Bir nechta xolos. Uchta, menimcha. Samsaga ko'p piyoz kerak.

lines.en: Is there any meat?
lines.uz: Go'sht bormi?

lines.en: Yes, there's a lot of meat. Mum bought two kilos yesterday.
lines.uz: Ha, go'sht ko'p. Oyim kecha ikki kilo olgandi.

lines.en: Good. So we need flour, onions and a little butter. Let's go to the shop!
lines.uz: Yaxshi. Demak, un, piyoz va ozgina sariyog' kerak. Do'konga ketdik!

steps.title_uz: much / many · a few / a little · a lot of
steps.body_uz:
**Sanaladigan** otlar (onions, eggs, apples) — **many**, **a few**, How **many**?
**Sanalmaydigan** otlar (flour, sugar, water, money) — **much**, **a little**, How **much**?
**a lot of** — ikkalasi bilan ham: a lot of onions, a lot of sugar. Darak gapda odatda **a lot of** ishlatiladi.
**much / many** asosan inkor va savolda: There isn't **much** milk. Have you got **many** friends?
**a few / a little** — "bir oz, bir nechta" (yetarli): I've got **a few** friends here.
Sanalmaydigan narsani sanash uchun: **a bottle of** water, **a kilo of** rice, **a cup of** tea.

examples.en: How many eggs do we need? — Six.
How much money have you got?
There isn't much milk in the fridge.
Add a little salt and a few tomatoes.
